items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Section headers and the 'weights sum to 16384, result >> 7' comments help, but there are cryptic names and magic shifts ('val', 's', 'temp', '262144 ... >> 19'), and the numerous scratch/*.py files make the change harder to follow.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: ~10 scratch/*.py debug scripts were committed along with a zig-out/lib/libswscale_candidate.so binary. scalePlane and scalePlanePacked duplicate the same two-pass logic, and scalePackedRgbAsPlanes is a third variant. The scalers are scalar loops, not shared @Vector helpers.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Allocations use try/defer free, which is good. But there are many magic constants (262144, >>19, >>7, 16384), and roundedDiv returns 'a' silently when b==0. The hidden tests also failed the accuracy bars.

items.name: Geometry, stride and tail handling
items.name_zh: 几何尺寸、步长与尾部处理
items.evidence: The output fails the hidden accuracy bars (score 0, correctness failed), so pixels are wrong on contract conversions. Kernels are scalar per-pixel loops with @min clamping, and chroma siting does not follow FFmpeg (the agent was still experimenting with it in scratch scripts).

items.name: ABI and build-target conformance
items.name_zh: ABI 与构建目标符合要求
items.evidence: The visible part of the diff suggests the Format/Algo enums match the API, but build.zig and the exports are not visible. The scalers allocate a temp buffer on every call inside process instead of precomputing it in create. The built .so was committed into zig-out.
